title: Stage 11 — Ship It
goal: Graduate Track 1: tests green locally and in CI, API and web deployed to public URLs, smoke-tested end to end.
summary: Run tests first, then deploy. The finale merges testing and deployment into one ship stage.

checkpoint.prompt: Before pushing or deploying, you run `npm test` locally. One test fails. What do you do first?

choices.text: Read the failure, fix code or test, re-run until green
Deploy anyway — CI will fix it
Delete the failing test file

checkpoint.explanation: Local red tests are cheaper than broken main. Fix before push.

checkpoint.prompt: In a unit test, what does the "assert" step do?

choices.text: Checks the outcome matches what you expected
Sets up the database
Deploys to production

checkpoint.explanation: Arrange sets up inputs, act runs the code under test, assert verifies the result.

checkpoint.prompt: Integration test: GET /me with no token expects 401. Admin route as user expects…

choices.text: 403 — authenticated but forbidden
200 — roles don't matter in tests
404 — user not found

checkpoint.explanation: Lock in auth sad paths so RBAC can't regress silently.

choices.text: In the host's environment / secrets UI — not in git
Committed to main in .env
Hardcoded in the frontend bundle

checkpoint.explanation: Secrets in git leak forever. Inject at deploy time.

checkpoint.prompt: After deploying, what is the simplest check that the API is alive? (one GET path)
checkpoint.explanation: A health endpoint confirms the process is up before you debug the full UI flow.

checklist.label: `npm test` passes locally including auth and pagination tests
Integration tests cover 401 (no token) and 403 (wrong role)
Test proves page 2 differs from page 1 when total > limit
Test covers at least one relation/join query from Stage 7
GitHub Actions runs tests on push — green on main
API and web on public HTTPS URLs in README
Created a record through the live site end to end

questions.prompt: Why run tests locally before deploying?

choices.text: Catch regressions cheaply before users or CI see broken code
Deploy automatically fails if you skip local tests
Tests replace the need for deployment

questions.explanation: Local green tests mean deploy and CI are validating known-good behavior.

questions.prompt: Unit test vs integration test — which hits real HTTP routes?

choices.text: Integration tests — supertest against the Express app
Unit tests — they always use fetch from the browser
Neither — Track 1 has no HTTP tests

questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise routing, middleware, and handlers together.

questions.prompt: Why test GET /workouts without a token expecting 401?

choices.text: Ensures auth middleware can't be accidentally removed
401 means the workout was not found
Tests should only cover happy paths

questions.explanation: Auth sad-path tests document security behavior you rely on.

questions.prompt: What belongs in production environment variables, not source code?

choices.text: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, WEB_URL for CORS
All React component names
Every route handler function

questions.explanation: Config and secrets differ per environment. Code stays the same.

choices.text: Live URLs, tests in CI, auth, and a full-stack app in one repo
Memorized every npm package
Finished without ever using Git branches

questions.explanation: Breadth + habits + one real shipped project. Specialization comes in Track 2.
